mcqs.question: Consider the following pairs of sets. Which pair consists of equal sets?
mcqs.explanation: Two sets are equal only when they contain exactly the same elements, irrespective of order or repetition. Option A lists the same three elements in both sets, so they are equal. The other options either have different elements or different cardinalities, so they are not equal.

mcqs.question: If set A = {1,2,3,4} and set B = {a,b,c,d}, which statement about their equivalence is correct?

options.A: They are equivalent because they have the same number of elements.
options.B: They are not equivalent because they contain different types of elements.
options.C: They are equivalent because they contain the same elements.
options.D: They are not equivalent because one is a subset of the other.

mcqs.answer: They are equivalent because they have the same number of elements.
mcqs.explanation: Two sets are equivalent when they have the same cardinality (the same number of elements), regardless of what the elements actually are. Both sets contain four elements, so they are equivalent. Options B, C, and D misuse the definition of equivalence.

mcqs.question: What is the standard notation used to denote the empty set?
mcqs.explanation: The universally accepted symbol for the empty set is the null set symbol ∅. While {} also represents an empty set, the question asks for the standard notation, which is ∅. Options A and D do not denote an empty set.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets is an example of a finite set?
mcqs.explanation: A finite set contains a limited number of elements. Option B lists exactly five numbers, making it finite. Option A and C describe infinite collections, and although the empty set {} is technically finite, the question seeks a non‑empty example, so B is the best choice.

mcqs.question: An infinite set is best described as:

options.A: A set with a countable number of elements.
options.B: A set that contains all real numbers.
options.C: A set that has no elements.
options.D: A set with an unbounded number of elements, i.e., not finite.

mcqs.answer: A set with an unbounded number of elements, i.e., not finite.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, an infinite set is one that is not finite; it has no bound on the number of its elements. Option D captures this definition. Option A describes a countably infinite set, which is a special case, but D is the broader correct description. Options B and C are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following sets is a singleton set?
mcqs.explanation: A singleton set contains exactly one element. Option B has precisely one element, 7, making it a singleton. Option A is empty, while C and D contain more than one element.

mcqs.question: Given Set M = {x | x is a vowel in the English alphabet} and Set N = {a, e, i, o, u}, which statement is true?

options.A: M and N are equal sets.
options.B: M is a proper subset of N.
options.C: N is a proper subset of M.

mcqs.answer: M and N are equal sets.
mcqs.explanation: Both M and N contain exactly the same five vowel letters, so they are equal sets. A proper subset would have fewer elements, and disjoint sets share no elements, which is not the case here.

mcqs.question: A teacher writes down the roll numbers of students present on Monday as set P = {1,2,3,4,5}. On Tuesday, she records the names of students present as set Q = {Alice, Bob, Carol, Dave, Eve}. Assuming each roll number corresponds uniquely to a name, what can be said about sets P and Q?

options.A: They are equivalent because both contain five elements.
options.B: They are equal because they contain the same elements.
options.C: They are disjoint because numbers and names are different.
options.D: P is a subset of Q.

mcqs.answer: They are equivalent because both contain five elements.
mcqs.explanation: Equivalence of sets depends only on cardinality. Both P and Q have five distinct elements, so they are equivalent. They are not equal because the actual elements differ, and they are not disjoint or subsets of each other.
